story.headline: Oura confidentially files for $11B IPO
story.summary: Ring-maker Oura filed confidential S-1 paperwork for a U.S. listing at an $11B target valuation, sources told Reuters.
story.source_excerpt: Oura Health has filed confidentially for a U.S. initial public offering at a valuation of about $11 billion, according to people familiar with the matter. The company filed an S-1 registration statement under the confidential treatment provision.
implications: Ring makers should map Oura's payments-tile roadmap against their own devices
Health-platform teams gain a public-comp valuation anchor for the ring form factor

story.headline: EU finalizes Digital Identity certification framework
story.summary: The European Commission published the final eIDAS 2.0 certification spec, requiring compliant national digital ID apps by October 2027.
story.source_excerpt: Today the European Commission has published the final implementing acts for the European Digital Identity framework. Member states must offer compliant digital ID apps to all citizens by October 2027.
implications: Any EU digital-ID app launch must include eIDAS 2.0 readiness from day one
Cross-border verifiable-credential support is now a 12-month requirement

story.summary: California registered nurses earn a median $67 per hour — the highest in the US.

California is the only state with a legally mandated nurse-to-patient ratio law. Urban centers like San Francisco, Los Angeles and San Diego have even higher pay rates.
implications: California's mandated nurse-to-patient ratios support these wages

story.headline: New grad nurse wages flat in real terms
story.summary: Today's new grads earn a national median of $28 per hour, according to Nurse.org.
story.source_excerpt: In nominal terms, new grad starting wages have grown nearly 10x since the 1960s. But in 2026 dollars, a new grad nurse in the 1970s earned the equivalent of ~$30/hr. Today's new grads, based on respondents, earn $28/hr. That's a slight decline in real purchasing power. The 2020s bucket reflects a range among respondents: reported new grad wages span roughly $22/hr in rural Oklahoma to $32–$47/hr in higher cost-of-living markets like New Jersey and California.
implications: Target higher cost-of-living markets to beat the median
